decisions.reason: Define-XML ADSL.VISNUMEN and workbook Methods!D133 literally select DSTERM='PROTCOL COMPLETED'; adsl-probe.yaml P4_COMPLETE and VISNUMEN preserve that spelling and the visit remapping. The staged DS has no matching term, so the reported missing probe values against nonmissing reference visits follow from the rule as written.

Define-XML ADSL.TRTSDT specifies SV.SVSTDTC at VISITNUM=3. The executable EX_MINDTC and TRTSDT elements instead take MIN(EX.EXSTDTC), so the documented source and visit condition have no executable counterpart.
Define-XML ADSL.TRTEDT names EXENDTC on the subject's last EX record. EX_MAXDTC filters on EXDOSE/EXTRT and maximizes end dates, which is a different selection rule even where its result agrees.

Define-XML ADSL.TRTEDT permits discontinuation-date substitution when the final dose date is missing and discontinuation is after visit 3. TRTEDT also caps an observed later exposure date and responds to any qualifying missing end date, without the documented visit condition.

Define-XML ADSL.CUMDOSE states arm-specific dose calculations over visit-delimited intervals. The full _CUM_CLOSED/_OPEN_TOTAL/_CUM0/_OPEN0 chain instead sums exposure-record dose-days and extends open records, so it does not express those documented interval conditions.

Define-XML ADSL.AGEGR1 explicitly names ADSL.AGEGR1N as the character-group predecessor. AGEGR1 uses DM.AGE and AGEGR1N is subsequently derived from AGEGR1, reversing that documented source direction.

The AGEGR1 and AGEGR1N elements together implement the age thresholds and numeric codes in Define-XML ADSL.AGEGR1N: AGEGR1 computes the age bracket and AGEGR1N maps that bracket to its code. Using this intermediate does not by itself omit or change the documented threshold computation; the reversed predecessor direction is separately captured by ADSL.AGEGR1.CR-6.1.

Define-XML ADSL.SAFFL requires ITTFL='Y' as well as a nonmissing treatment start. SAFFL tests only TRTSDT presence, and the dataset's Screen Failure filter does not express the missing ARMCD/ITTFL condition.

Define-XML ADSL.COMP8FL requires an end-date comparison to the visit date. N_WK8 only counts visit records and COMP8FL only tests that count, with no end-date comparison elsewhere in their executable chain.
Define-XML ADSL.COMP16FL requires ENDDT to reach the visit date. N_WK16 and COMP16FL use only visit-record presence and contain no counterpart to that comparison.
Define-XML ADSL.COMP24FL requires ENDDT to reach the visit date. N_WK24 and COMP24FL use only visit-record presence and contain no counterpart to that comparison.

Define-XML ADSL.DISCONFL compares the grouped reason DCREASCD with Completed, whereas DISCONFL compares EOSSTT derived from DCDECOD. The DCSREAS method link identifies the legacy grouped reason, but it does not turn the implemented status comparison into a comparison of that reason, which the specification leaves blank for completed subjects.

Define-XML ADSL.DSRAEFL compares the grouped reason DCREASCD with Adverse Event. DSRAEFL instead directly tests DCDECOD, bypassing DCSREAS and its source selection and override; the DCSREAS-to-DCREASCD method link resolves the legacy name but does not remove that source difference.

Define-XML ADSL.DTHFL and the executable DTHFL element both read DM.DTHFL. The CASE preserves every nonmissing source value and represents missing character values as an empty string, so the automatic failure to resolve a plain-copy expression does not establish a different copy source.
Define-XML ADSL.DURDIS names DISONSET, while _DURDIS_DAYS starts at DISONSDT. The retained ADSL inventory and workbook give no DISONSET variable or metadata link equating these names.
Define-XML ADSL.DURDSGR1 describes a >=12 group. The DURDSGR1 otherwise branch also assigns that group when DURDIS is missing, so its condition is broader than the documented threshold.
Define-XML ADSL.RFENDTC names DM.RFENDTC. The RFENDTC element instead chooses between DS_ENDTC and SV_SCHED_ENDTC, which resolve to DS and SV rather than the documented DM source.

Define-XML ADSL.VISNUMEN selects completion disposition records and remaps the final visit. VISNUMEN instead maximizes scheduled SV visits within its cutoff, without the documented DS source or completion-term condition.

Define-XML ADSL.DCSREAS says to group DCDECOD values. DCSREAS reads DS_DISP.DSDECOD selected first by date, while DCDECOD reads DS_LAST.DSDECOD selected last, so the implemented source-selection logic differs even though the staged category is unique per subject.
Define-XML ADSL.MMSETOT names QS.QSORRES. MMSETOT sums QS.QSSTRESN instead; the original and standardized result variables remain different documented sources even where their numeric values agree.

Define-XML ADSL.MMSETOT specifies QSCAT=MINI-MENTAL STATE. The executable MMSETOT filter adds a visit restriction and uses the MMITM test-code prefix instead of the category condition, changing the record-selection rule.

Original Define-XML IT.ADSL.STUDYID contains a Predecessor Origin description DM.STUDYID at line 596; workbook Variables!M143/P143 confirms it. The exported ADSL.STUDYID section omitted that origin, so this derivation is documented.

Original Define-XML IT.ADSL.USUBJID contains a Predecessor Origin description DM.USUBJID at line 607; workbook Variables!M144/P144 confirms it. The exported ADSL.USUBJID section omitted that origin, so this derivation is documented.

Define-XML ADSL.SITEGR1 and workbook Methods!D122 state the pooled/unpooled outputs and refer to SAP Section 7.1, but neither identifies the fixed site set in SITEGR1. The retained study sections contain no such set, and the shared SAP applicability remains pending in the source manifest.

Define-XML ADSL.SITEGR1 and workbook Methods!D122 do not specify which sites are pooled. The source manifest leaves the shared SAP applicability pending, so the retained governing rule does not supply a literal pooling condition.

Define-XML ADSL.TRTSDT specifies conversion to a SAS date, without month/day completion. Neither the workbook method nor the retained reviewer guide states January/day-1 imputation for this variable; the guide page-5 imputation rule explicitly concerns ADAE.ASTDT.

Original Define-XML ItemRef IT.ADSL.TRTDURD (lines 209-210) and workbook Variables!O155 bind the legacy TRTDUR method to TRTDURD. Define-XML ADSL.CUMDOSE and Methods!D99 still leave ARMN and TRTSTDT unbound, and the ARMN codelist gives randomized-dose codes rather than the arm numbering required by the formula, so a literal probe still needs source and mapping choices.

Define-XML ADSL.COMP8FL and workbook Methods!D98 require ENDDT but do not define it or link it to a published ADSL date. Searching the retained sections and workbook finds no definition supplying that necessary comparison source.
Define-XML ADSL.COMP16FL and workbook Methods!D96 require ENDDT but do not define it or link it to a published ADSL date. No retained section or workbook definition resolves that source.
Define-XML ADSL.COMP24FL and workbook Methods!D97 require ENDDT but do not define it or link it to a published ADSL date. No retained section or workbook definition resolves that source.

Define-XML ADSL.BMIBL and workbook Methods!D94 state the height conversion and squared denominator without zero-height handling. Neither the retained sections nor the workbook states the explicit NULLIF guard in _BMIBL_RAW.

Define-XML ADSL.HEIGHTBL and workbook Methods!D112 specify the test and visit but no date ordering or repeated-measurement selection. No retained section supplies the earliest-date/first-record rule in BASE_HT.

Define-XML ADSL.WEIGHTBL and workbook Methods!D134 specify the test and visit but no date ordering or repeated-measurement selection. No retained section supplies the earliest-date/first-record rule in BASE_WT.

Define-XML ADSL.EDUCLVL and workbook Methods!D108 identify EDLEVEL without a date-based selection rule. The retained sections contain no counterpart to SC_EDU ordering by SCDTC and taking the first record.

Define-XML ADSL.DISONSDT and workbook Methods!D103 state date conversion without completing missing components. No retained section states June/day-15 completion for disease-onset dates; the reviewer guide imputation discussion applies to ADAE.ASTDT.

Define-XML ADSL.DISONSDT and workbook Methods!D103 identify the primary-diagnosis history category but do not choose among its records. No retained section states the MH_DX earliest-onset/first-record convention.

Define-XML ADSL.DURDIS and workbook Methods!D106 describe months between two dates without inclusive day counting. The retained sections contain no counterpart to the closed-both day difference in _DURDIS_DAYS.
Define-XML ADSL.DURDIS and workbook Methods!D106 do not define the length of a month or an average-year conversion. No retained section states the multiplier and divisor in _DURDIS_MONTHS.

Define-XML ADSL.DURDIS and workbook Methods!D106 leave DISONSET unresolved and do not specify the month-count arithmetic. Neither the ADSL inventory nor another retained section supplies those missing source and computation definitions.
Define-XML ADSL.VISIT1DT and workbook Methods!D132 state SAS date conversion without completing missing components. No retained section documents the January/day-1 completion in VISIT1DT.
Define-XML ADSL.VISIT1DT and workbook Methods!D132 specify the visit and source without ordering repeated records. The retained sections contain no counterpart to SV_V1 choosing the earliest SVSTDTC.

Define-XML ADSL.DCDECOD and workbook Methods!D100 identify disposition-event records but state no date order or last-record rule. DS_LAST adds that general selection convention, even though it has no effect where the staged qualifying record is unique.

Define-XML ADSL.DCSREAS and workbook Methods!D101 say to group DCDECOD, while the DISCREAS codelist only enumerates codes and decodes. Neither they nor another retained section state the DSTERM-based protocol-entry override in DCSREAS.

Define-XML ADSL.DCSREAS and its DISCREAS codelist include Completed but do not state that completed subjects receive an empty reason. The workbook repeats the grouping statement and supplies no counterpart to the empty-string branch.

Define-XML ADSL.DCSREAS and workbook Methods!D101 state grouping, and the codelist supplies output values and decodes, but they do not completely define the grouping or completed-subject handling. The metadata link resolves the legacy DCREASCD method name without supplying these missing conditions.

Define-XML ADSL.DISCONFL and workbook Methods!D102 compare the grouped reason with Completed, and original Define-XML ItemRef IT.ADSL.DCSREAS (lines 275-276) plus Variables!O190 bind the legacy DCREASCD method to DCSREAS. The probe preserves that source and the SAS-style inequality for blank reasons, explaining the reported Y values where the reference flag is empty.

Define-XML ADSL.EFFFL and workbook Methods!D109 require a post-baseline ADAS-Cog questionnaire record, while original SDTM Define QS.QSTESTCD.ACTOT identifies ACTOT as the ADAS-COG(11) subscore. N_ACTOT restricts eligibility to that total rather than any record for the documented questionnaire, and no retained rule supplies that restriction.

Define-XML ADSL.DISCONFL and workbook Methods!D102 say Null otherwise without requiring a physical Parquet null, and ADRG page-36 discusses null and empty text as missing-value representations. The staged SAS-transport reference stores unpopulated DISCONFL as empty text, so the specification's empty-string branch does not establish a different character-flag rule.

Define-XML ADSL.EFFFL and workbook Methods!D109 already require a post-baseline CIBIC+ record; original SDTM Define ValueList.QS.QSTESTCD and ItemDef QS.QSTESTCD.CIBIC (lines 5697-5705) identify the CIBIC question and its response codelist. Together with the QSCAT codelist's CIBIC+ questionnaire name, these provide a counterpart for N_CIBIC's short-code selection rather than an additional undocumented eligibility condition.

missed.quote: All patients in DM were included in ADSL.
missed.reason: No claim cites this dataset-population statement; the specification filters DM.ACTARM to exclude Screen Failure. Original Define-XML IG.ADSL def:Structure at line 182 and workbook Datasets!D5 instead explicitly exclude Screen Failures, so this statement also needs document-to-document reconciliation.
